ideas.risks: The second clean sample is also hidden, so the argument may collapse back to exponential mask enumeration or anti-hitting. Arbitrary weak learners can overfit the generation sample, and this still may not solve final sparse-majority selection.
ideas.summary: Try to reorganize the DCHP-style proof with two independent hidden-clean roles: one sample/transcript generates a bag, while an independent ghost clean sample certifies population performance on D_c^+. The explorer should state exact independence and mask-discovery requirements, then prove a transfer theorem or isolate the exponential step.
ideas.title: Ghost-Sample Clean Transfer
ideas.why_promising: This attacks the current middle bottleneck directly: clean-population transfer. If independence can be made real, finite-class or compression arguments become available.

ideas.risks: The good vote may have exponentially small measure under any natural sampler. Set-Cover-style examples suggest random sparse majorities usually miss rare covers. Clean validation labels are unavailable.
ideas.summary: Replace exact ERM over sign(B^(T)) by a randomized polynomial final list. Given a generated bag B, sample T-wise majorities from uniform, frequency-weighted, or boosting-induced distributions and ask whether an accurate clean-conditional vote appears with inverse-polynomial probability.
ideas.title: Random Vote Lists
ideas.why_promising: It bypasses the known Set-Cover hardness of exact sparse-majority ERM and would plug directly into the clean-list sufficiency lemma.

ideas.risks: The atlas source does not imply stability or compression; rare-slice junk refutes black-box range control. The assumptions may be nearly as strong as the desired conclusion, and the selector problem can remain separate.
ideas.summary: Formulate a conditional positive theorem under natural regularity of the supplied weak learner: leave-one-out stability on low-OPT calls, small transcript compression, or distribution-dependent range quotients. Determine which assumptions suffice for CleanPopulationTransfer and which also give a polynomial final list.
ideas.title: Stable Weak Learner Route
ideas.why_promising: It turns the vague controlled-range hope into precise, checkable hypotheses and could yield a meaningful conditional atlas implication.

ideas.risks: A restricted oracle theorem will not be an atlas separation. Returned hypothesis handles may leak large information, and public constants, spikes, and other witnesses must be routed explicitly.
ideas.summary: Build a stopped-process random-hidden-target model where target-useful low-OPT queries require transcript information about the hidden target or clean mask. Include a query grammar, canonical dummy replies on the hard band, public-witness routing, and an information budget for oracle outputs.
ideas.title: Stopped Public-Posterior Barrier
ideas.why_promising: It could convert the many residual/filtering obstructions into one rigorous black-box lower-bound statement, clarifying exactly what any positive proof must escape.

ideas.risks: It may remain an artificial selector warning only. Literal DCHP compatibility is threatened by spike tuple calls, final-mass versus weak-lightness tension, adaptive key leakage, and extra columns destroying no-instances.
ideas.summary: Prove a standalone query-light generated-bag theorem: if every weak-call distribution places at most tau < beta mass on a common block S, a valid weak learner can program arbitrary Set-Cover columns on S while preserving OPT+beta. Track confidence, key-hit probability, extra columns, and final-sample relevance.
ideas.title: Query-Light Bag Pollution
ideas.why_promising: This would precisely delimit when generated bags cannot be assumed benign and would sharpen criticism of black-box final-selector primitives.

ideas.risks: Distribution-free weighted low-noise weak decoding may already be hard. Many local/list decoding theorems assume uniform coordinates or random errors, and classical decoding hardness does not rule out improper prediction.
ideas.summary: Search for succinct codeword classes over exponential coordinate domains with efficient low-noise weak/approximate decoding under arbitrary coordinate marginals, but hard high-noise RCN improper prediction. Test Reed-Muller, BCH, locally decodable, and list-decodable families against the weighted weak-learning requirement.
ideas.title: Succinct Code Candidates
ideas.why_promising: This is a non-parity version of the remaining plausible negative template: easy below gamma, hard in the hard band.

ideas.risks: Fixed-arity domains are table-learnable, public RHS encodings are trivial, and low-noise weak learning can itself solve the intended hard prediction problem. Known hardness may be only proper, search, or refutation hardness.
ideas.summary: Audit non-parity approximation-gap candidates with efficient constant-factor or additive agnostic approximation and suspected OPT+epsilon improper hardness, such as signed cut, synchronization, or low-rank predicate classes with succinct descriptor domains. For each, apply the L029 weak-side conversion and the eta < gamma stress test.
ideas.title: Non-Parity Gap Search
ideas.why_promising: After sparse XOR failed, this is still the cleanest conditional separation route if an independent low-noise approximator can be found.
